sources.finding: NASM hip-flexor stretching uses a supported half-kneeling position with posterior pelvic tilt; the couch variant increases knee/hip-flexor range while remaining supported.

sources.title: Crab Walk Exercise
sources.finding: ACE animal-flow guidance uses crab locomotion with hands and feet supporting the body, hips elevated and coordinated opposite-limb movement, combining upper-body/core strength with coordination.

sources.title: Core Programming That Translates to Real Life
sources.finding: NASM uses cable lifts/chops as rotational core patterns that transfer force between lower and upper body and require controlled trunk rotation.

sources.title: Cable Crossover
sources.finding: NASM classifies cable crossover advanced and prescribes a stable staggered stance, braced core and controlled shoulder arc without excessive hyperextension.

sources.title: Dumbbell Bench Press
sources.finding: ACE dumbbell chest-press guidance uses a supported supine bench position, controlled shoulder/elbow motion and stable wrist alignment; close grip changes arm position but not the supported base.

sources.title: Running Basics and Training
sources.finding: ACE presents continuous running as a fundamental locomotor cardiovascular activity, progressing duration gradually with relaxed efficient form rather than complex technique.

sources.title: Running Basics and Training
sources.finding: ACE presents distance running as fundamental cardiovascular locomotion, with gradual volume progression and efficient relaxed running mechanics.

sources.title: Interval Training
sources.finding: ACE interval running alternates harder running bouts with recovery periods; complexity comes from pacing/intensity changes rather than advanced movement skill.

sources.title: Cable Triceps Extension
sources.finding: NASM cable triceps-extension guidance emphasizes controlled elbow extension and stable scapular positioning; cross-body direction changes cable path without requiring exceptional range.

sources.title: Rotational Training Plans — Standing Cable Chest Press
sources.finding: NASM describes standing cable chest press as a free-standing press where cable direction creates a stability/anti-rotation demand, with controlled forward pressing.

sources.title: Barbell Biceps Curl
sources.finding: ACE barbell curl uses a stable standing base, neutral wrists, fixed upper arms and controlled elbow flexion/extension; it is an isolated arm exercise without complex balance.

sources.title: Biceps Curl
sources.finding: ACE dumbbell biceps curl uses upright posture, elbows close to the torso and controlled elbow flexion, with no exceptional mobility or balance component.

sources.title: Hammer Curl
sources.finding: NASM hammer curl is a beginner isolated elbow-flexion exercise performed with neutral grip, stable posture and controlled range.

sources.title: Crow Pose
sources.finding: Crow is an arm-balance requiring weight transfer onto the hands, bent-arm support, hip mobility, core control and sustained balance; it is commonly taught as an intermediate arm balance.

sources.title: Hammer Curl
sources.finding: NASM hammer curl is a beginner isolated elbow-flexion exercise using neutral grip and controlled motion; cross-body direction does not require exceptional range.

sources.title: Straight-Arm Pulldown / Cable Pullover
sources.finding: ACE straight-arm cable pulldown uses stable standing posture and controlled shoulder extension from an overhead cable position while maintaining trunk alignment.

sources.title: Seated Row
sources.finding: ACE cable row guidance uses a stable seated position, neutral spine and controlled scapular/shoulder retraction; rear-delt emphasis changes elbow path rather than support demands.

sources.title: Shoulder Scaption
sources.finding: ACE scaption uses a stable standing base and controlled arm elevation in the scapular plane, emphasizing posture and shoulder control.

sources.title: Dead Bug
sources.finding: NASM describes dead bug as an accessible all-levels supine core-stability exercise with controlled contralateral arm/leg motion while maintaining trunk position.

sources.title: Triceps Dip
sources.finding: ACE parallel-bar triceps dip requires supporting full bodyweight through the arms, controlled elbow/shoulder flexion and stable suspended body position.

sources.title: Bodyweight Squat
sources.finding: ACE squat guidance requires controlled bilateral stance and alignment through hip/knee flexion; a sustained deep position increases positional control demand but does not add external load.

sources.title: Lunge Variations
sources.finding: ACE lunge progressions emphasize single-leg stability, controlled stepping/lowering and mastery of bodyweight patterns before added resistance; cross-behind direction increases multiplanar control.
